Title: Toward a European Fiscal Community: Treaty Design and Club Formation

Description: Europe’s fiscal stalemate rests on a premise: that a fiscal union must include its most creditworthy members—the “frugals”—from day one, and must be diluted until they consent. We invert the premise. A fiscal community of the willing pays even without the frugals, and their very absence disciplines it, as the quality of common spending becomes the currency with which their entry is bought. We give this idea a legal and institutional form: the European Fiscal Community (EFC), established by an international treaty outside the EU framework, with a federal executive elected by an interparliamentary assembly, and a common bond financing growth-oriented European public goods. Our contribution is twofold. First, we draft the full treaty and ensure its compatibility with EU primary law and national constitutional law. Second, we develop a game-theoretic model in which spending quality is chosen under a common-pool distortion, but the prospect of accession generates a recruitment dividend that disciplines insiders. Two stable equilibria emerge, selected by expectations about enlargement, with sharp design implications: independent evaluation, conditional scaling rules, and a portfolio that starts with excludable club goods. A calibration exercise prices the funding cost of the bond under alternative club compositions: a fiscal community can start without Germany, and German accession is the prize that disciplines it until quality is locked in by institutional design.

Title: Auctioning Attention on Social Networks

Description: Social media recommendation systems create conflict: content producers, content consumers, platform operators, and social pressures struggle to direct the allocation of attention in their favor while also facing competing societal pressures. Producers may feel pressure to optimize for recommendation algorithms and consumers may be exposed to content with negative externalities such as polarization and misinformation. Platforms aim to maximize user engagement, oftentimes resulting in over consumption from consumers. There is mounting pressure from policymakers and broader society to address these issues. Prior methods for constructing social media feeds have focused on recommendation systems. Instead, we propose a, to our knowledge, novel auction based method for feed construction where users bid for the attention of other users. Our mechanism systematically considers producers, consumers, platform operators, and social welfare. We show that our auction is weakly incentive compatible in expectation under budget constraints with myopic agents and optimizes producer welfare. To balance between producer and consumer welfare, we introduce a tax policy to the auction to increase the cost of content with negative externalities. Simulations over common social network topologies and an empirically observed network show how different feed algorithms prioritize different stakeholders. Our proposed auction based mechanisms produce on average 36.3% higher producer welfare than comparison algorithms on the empirically observed network. Additionally, our methods produce 31.4% higher producer welfare than comparison algorithms on the synthetic networks. Our methods also produce consistently more equitable distributions of attention than baseline methods across all evaluated network types. Addressing all stakeholders is difficult; the incentives of each stakeholder are often mutually incompatible. Our proposed mechanism addresses attention allocation at a systematic level, balancing between the needs of different stakeholders.

Title: The Reader Is the Variable Constraint Factorization, Free Moves, and Instrument Limits in Deterministic Transformation Fields

Description: The Reader Is the Variable

Constraint Factorization, Free Moves, and Instrument Limits in Deterministic Transformation Fields

Driven by Dean A. Kulik

September 2026

Abstract

This paper audits a deterministic transformation field for structure that survives the removal of reader-side artifacts. Four channels previously treated as primitive — position, adjacency, value, and echo — reduce to two: value is the output of a read rule applied to structure, and an echo is that read rule failing to separate two structurally distinct states. The remaining primitives are position and adjacency, an unlabeled relational graph.

Two consequences are forced by this reduction and both correct previously stated architecture. First, a stateless reader cannot detect the convergence criterion the architecture specifies: periodicity is a property of a sequence, not of an output, so the reader must be a transducer carrying at least as much state as the return period. Second, under the corrected relational form of C0, return period is the only observable in the current vocabulary that is natively two-frame; every other candidate — band width, echo position, fiber size, value — is a single-frame reading requiring an externally supplied comparison.

The central computation is a factorization audit of the SHA-256 dependency lattice. The Davies–Meyer feed-forward separates the digest constraint into eight independent 32-bit conditions. That separation is destroyed by a single backward round: the ancestry of the last schedule word is the complete seed. Forward, the picture inverts — ten expanded words carry partial ancestry, with full coupling first reached at W[26]. The two factorizations do not meet. Under a single varying seed word the invariant cone contains exactly two expanded words, {16,17}, which coincides with a seam previously derived from an unrelated dual-rail criterion.

Four measured instrument failures are reported as constraints rather than discarded. Each shares one defect: a relational structure was reduced to a scalar before being tested for relational content. A canonical-section theorem is derived limiting any deterministic recovery procedure to at most one preimage per collision fiber, which sharpens the admissible-domain condition from smallness to sectionhood. Falsifiers are given for each surviving claim, including a base-scaling test that would reverse the four-to-two reduction.

Title: Freshwater Resources: A Critical Factor Guiding Earth's Future

Description: Abstract

Freshwater is one of the most important natural resources on Earth and may become the most valuable resource in the future. Freshwater can be defined as water that contains less than 1,000 milligrams per liter of dissolved solids . Only about 2% of the Earth’s total water is freshwater. It is essential for all land, aquatic, and marine life, including humans. Due to population growth, climate change, pollution, and the declining level of groundwater, pressure on this limited resource is increasing. As a result, the shortage of freshwater may become more severe in the future. This paper discusses the sources, importance, causes, and impacts of freshwater shortage, and possible solutions.

Keywords : Population growth, climate change, freshwater resources, freshwater shortage .

Title: Determinantes gravitacionales y competitividad de las agroexportaciones no tradicionales peruanas (1999-2024)

Description: El objetivo de este artículo es analizar los determinantes gravitacionales y la competitividad de las agroexportaciones no tradicionales peruanas (arándano, palta, mango y uva) entre 1999 y 2024. Desde la gerencia estratégica, la investigación adopta un enfoque cuantitativo, explicativo y longitudinal. Se construyó un panel de datos macroeconómico bilateral, procesado mediante el estimador estructural Pseudo Poisson Maximum Likelihood (PPML), garantizando inferencias consistentes ante flujos comerciales nulos y heterocedasticidad. Los resultados del modelo base demuestran que el tamaño del mercado de destino (PBI) impulsa significativamente las exportaciones con una elasticidad de 0.528, mientras que la distancia física ejerce una severa fricción estructural con un coeficiente penalizador de -0.767. Asimismo, la vigencia de los Tratados de Libre Comercio (TLC) constituye el principal catalizador institucional con un coeficiente de 1.444, el cual se estabiliza de forma robusta en 0.618 al controlar por efectos fijos de año y producto. Por el contrario, se identificó una profunda penalización en el nivel de valor agregado (-2.915), evidenciando empíricamente que la ventaja competitiva del sector permanece anclada en la exportación en fresco debido al bajo escalonamiento industrial.

Title: The Luminous Prosperity Model Limitations Disclosure: Instrument 05 of the Luminous Governance Framework

Description: Every other instrument in the Luminous Governance Framework specifies what an AI system will do. This one specifies what it cannot do, may not attempt, and must never say. It is a negative specification — a governance instrument defined entirely by its prohibitions — and it operationalises the framework's fourth pillar, epistemic humility.
The governing argument is stated plainly: a system that cannot say what it does not know will be believed about things it does not know. Silence about limitation is not neutrality but a claim, and users fill that silence generously because machine output arrives fluent, immediate, and confident. This instrument therefore publishes the incapacity of the system in the same register, with the same specificity, and in the same places as its capability.
Section II states the epistemic position honestly: a developmental inference is a probabilistic pattern-match over language and behaviour, produced by models trained on culturally situated data, evaluated against developmental frameworks that are themselves contested instruments. Section III enumerates ten classes of thing the system cannot know, including actual developmental stage as distinct from a correlated signal, interior experience and felt sense, intention, the truth of self-report, trauma history, clinical status, future trajectory, the valence of change, spiritual condition, and a person's worth or ceiling. Section IV enumerates eight categorically prohibited inference classes — clinical diagnosis, suicide and self-harm risk scoring, protected-characteristic inference, political affiliation, criminality propensity, employability and creditworthiness and insurability, parental and relational fitness — governed by a general test: any inference whose primary use would be to make a decision about a person rather than to offer something to them is forbidden. Section V prohibits six classes of speech act and supplies a binding required-language table of fifteen prohibited/required pairs written to be usable directly by engineers and copywriters.
Section VI specifies the mandatory user-facing uncertainty affordance. Section VII is an honest register of seven known failure modes with mitigations, marked where mitigation is only partial. Section VIII states without softening that stage-model measurement validity is disputed in the peer-reviewed literature, that Spiral Dynamics has essentially no peer-reviewed validation record, and that the system's constraints are designed on the assumption that its own instruments may be wrong. Sections IX and X establish disclosure obligations and Governance Circle enforcement, including the operative rule that no inference class enters production before it is added to this register.

Title: The TripleBird Project – Bending the curve of biodiversity. Securing the future.

Description: The TripleBird project builds a bridge between biodiversity monitoring and effective conservation action. Together with partners from science and practice, we generate robust insights for assessing and protecting biodiversity. TripleBird combines three core components: BirdTwin serves as the foundation as a digital twin based on bird monitoring and environmental data; BirdFutures develops models and scenarios through co-design with stakeholders from business, conservation, and the financial sector; and BirdBusiness supports applications in companies and financial institutions. Together, these three pillars aim to enable a comprehensive assessment of the current state of biodiversity, the early detection of emerging developments, the targeted evaluation of measures, and thus the effective support of practical conservation efforts.

Title: Il divario tra valori e azione: la de-bolezza della volontà e un modello antropologico integrato

Description: Nel dibattito contemporaneo sull’agency umana, accanto al polo dell’integrazione basata su modelli normativi/etici come, per esempio, il modello di Stephen Covey in The 8th Habit: From Effectiveness to Greatness (2004), troviamo il polo della critica/denuncia sociologica, esemplificato ne Il libro delle emozioni (2021) da Umberto Galimberti. I lavori di Magda Arnold (1903-2002) e, in particolare, di Antonio Damasio (1944) costituiscono una sorta di terzo polo dell’integrazione neurobiologica. Rifiutando il dualismo cartesiano, e mostrando le radici profonde nell’architettura neurale del problema sociologico, Damasio spiega la necessità dell’integrazione tra le risposte emotive corporee e la mente. Intendiamo sviluppare un modello interpretativo della persona che integri la cruciale distinzione tra emozioni e sentimenti, ponendola in dialogo con la razionalità e la storia personale. Il modello potrà illuminare il frequente divario tra le aspirazioni valoriali coltivate nello “spirito” del soggetto e la debolezza della volontà nell’azione concreta (acrasia). La mancata integrazione tra emozioni, sentimenti, ragione, storia e identità ostacola, infatti, la fioritura umana. L’applicazione del modello alla gestione dei conflitti interpersonali mostrerà la sua utilità per la praxis etica.

Title: Hyperbolic Completion, Ordered Ratio Transport, and the Critical Jordan-Strip Variation Obstruction (PIHR-RH XXXIV)

Description: This thirty-fourth PIHR-RH manuscript records the progress obtained after PIHR-RH XXXIII. The starting point of PIHR-RH XXXIII was the identification of an ordered first-order ratio transport with the correct harmonic prime-spine normalization, together with the warning that the commutator-matching theorem had not yet been proved. The present stage continues precisely at that remaining point. Several candidate matching identities are audited coefficientwise. The naive primewise identification of the XXXII overdiagonal commutator with the XXXIII centered ordered transport is rejected. In its place, an exact hyperbolic completion identity is obtained. The overdiagonal ratio shell is shown to be one side of a causal/anti-causal hyperbola split, and its Peano ratio derivative admits a one-sided causal funding inequality depending only on the unconditional positivity of the reciprocal von Mangoldt deficit.

The main new structural conclusions are: (i) the XXXII shell is exactly a difference of two nonnegative Selberg-type deficits with identical equilibrium mode; (ii) the correct comparison is not a scalar positivity argument but an antisymmetric first-order ordered transport; (iii) the endpoint/history structure of the XXVI largest-prime/least-prime resolvent intertwines exactly with the XXXIII two-parameter ratio deformation; (iv) prime-power and post-spine contributions are subexponential or bounded and therefore cannot carry the final obstruction; (v) the remaining term is the centered barycentric crossing moment, equivalently the neutral derivative of a critical Jordan-strip homotopy. A Peano-integrated beta-curvature decomposition further shows that the genuine multi-prime sector has nonnegative contribution, while the diagonal sector reduces to an explicitly bounded constant after the harmonic prime-spine cancellation.

Despite these advances, the manuscript does not claim a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. The final unresolved theorem is now sharply localized: one must control the negative variation of the critical Jordan-strip evolution, or equivalently prove an ordered barycentric comparison for crossing episodes. This statement is precisely the place where an off-critical zero would produce exponential beta-variation. Thus the present manuscript narrows the remaining obstruction but does not remove it.

Title: Reawakening Ọkọnkọ: Indigenous Peace Architecture and Violence Prevention amongst the Ngwa-Igbo of Southeastern Nigeria

Description: ABSTRACT:

This study examined Ọkọnkọ as an indigenous peace architecture and its potential contribution to violence prevention amongst the Ngwa-Igbo of Southeastern Nigeria. Against the background of urbanisation, cultural transformation and the weakening of indigenous institutions, the study explored Ọkọnkọ's historical peacebuilding functions, contemporary community perceptions and prospects for responsible revitalisation. Guided by Indigenous Knowledge Systems and Restorative Justice theories, the study adopted a qualitative exploratory design. Fieldwork was conducted across four core Ngwa communities between October 2025 and January 2026. Participants were purposively and snowball-sampled and comprised traditional rulers, Ọkọnkọ members, community elders, youth leaders, security personnel and historians. Data were generated through 32 semi-structured in-depth interviews, non-participant observation and historical/documentary analysis. Data were analysed using content thematic analysis, with triangulation across individual narratives, observed practices and historical/documentary evidence. Findings indicate that Ọkọnkọ historically functioned as a multidimensional peace institution through mediation, customary adjudication, moral regulation, communal accountability and non-lethal sanctions. Its authority was rooted in cultural legitimacy and collective norms. Although its contemporary institutional influence has declined, participants perceived selected practices as potentially relevant to violence prevention and restorative community governance. The study contributes to decolonial peacebuilding scholarship by repositioning Ọkọnkọ as an endogenous peace architecture whose critically adapted principles can complement formal justice and security institutions.

Keywords: Ọkọnkọ; indigenous peacebuilding; restorative justice; violence prevention; Ngwaland.

Title: Containment by Design: A Layered Architecture and Open Testbed for Containing, Detecting and Recovering from Misbehaving LLM Agents

Description: LLM agents are now deployed with credentials, tools and long-running autonomy, and most 2026 incidents did not require a scheming model: an ordinary agent that cannot separate data from instructions was enough once composed into a system with too many permissions. This preprint argues for containment by design : building the harness first so it holds whether the agent is hijacked, confused or adversarial.
It contributes (1) a layered architecture of nine independent walls, (2) a six-step detection and recapture playbook for when the walls fail, modelled on how high-security prisons handle escapes, (3) an open, dependency-free testbed with eleven adversarial scenarios and a knock-one-out ablation method, and (4) a mapping to the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications. With all walls active every scenario is contained; with each primary wall removed a backup wall contains all ten adversarial cases; with every wall removed eight of eleven escape. The agents are scripted, so results validate harness logic and layer independence rather than attack success against real models.

Title: Metodo del punto di sella nel calcolo complesso

Description: Il metodo del punto di sella (noto anche come steepest descent ) costituisce un pilastro dell'analisi complessa e della fisica teorica per lo studio del comportamento asintotico di integrali dipendenti da un parametro reale o complesso grande. La memoria offre una trattazione completa del metodo, affrontandone la giustificazione geometrica legata all'armonicità della parte reale dell'esponente e alla struttura a sella dei suoi punti stazionari. Vengono forniti gli strumenti algebrici per la determinazione univoca della direzione di ripidissima discesa ( ) e lo sviluppo gaussiano locale al primo ordine e ad ordini superiori. La componente storica ripercorre le tappe cruciali della sua formulazione, evidenziando le radici reali in Laplace, i manoscritti inediti di Riemann (1863), i contributi di Nekrasov (1890) e la formalizzazione di Peter Debye (1909). A completamento della trattazione, vengono svolti nel dettaglio esempi didattici e applicativi di rilievo in meccanica quantistica, ottica ed elettrodinamica: dall'approssimazione di Stirling alle funzioni di Airy, fino allo studio delle funzioni di Bessel e delle funzioni di Hankel in prossimità del punto di svolta.

Title: The World After the Desire

Description: When desire is fully satisfied, it does not disappear. It transforms. This paper proposes that beyond the saturation of ordinary desire – for objects, power, recognition – a structural shift occurs: the emergence of what we term beyond-desire (oltre-desiderio), the impulse not to obtain the world but to shape it. This cosmogonic drive is not pathological. It is the oldest form of human agency, and it is now, for the first time in history, becoming technically achievable at scale through agentic artificial intelligence. The paper traces the trajectory from desire to beyond-desire, examines its structural logic through the lens of the Cognitive Governance Framework (CGF), and argues that AI governance must account not only for what systems do, but for the cosmogonic ambitions of those who build them.

Title: Decoding Soundscapes: Machine Learning Approaches for Speech-to-Text Conversion

Description: Abstract: The conversion of audio signals into text has become essential in human–computer interaction, accessibility, and information management. With the rise of multimedia and real-time communication, machine learning (ML) has revolutionized speech recognition by bridging spoken and written language more effectively than traditional rule-based systems. Modern ML models use supervised and unsupervised learning to process acoustic features such as MFCCs, spectrograms, and deep audio embeddings through architectures like RNNs, CNNs, and transformers, enabling accurate and context-aware transcription. End-to-end deep learning approaches, including sequence-to-sequence and attention mechanisms, have further enhanced performance by minimizing manual feature design. Advances in transfer learning, multilingual pre-training, and self-supervised learning have expanded speech recognition to low-resource languages, as demonstrated by large models like wav2vec and Whisper. These innovations have broad applications in voice assistants, captioning, healthcare documentation, legal and industrial transcription, and accessibility tools, delivering significant social and economic benefits. However, challenges such as noise, code-switching, domain adaptation, high computational demands, and ethical concerns related to privacy, bias, and fairness persist. Ongoing research focuses on improving the robustness, efficiency, and inclusivity of ML-based speech recognition systems for universal and responsible deployment.

Title: Beyond Random Assignment: A Pedagogical & AI Ecosystem for Scalable Capstone Team Formation

Description: We present an end-to-end pedagogical and AI ecosystem designed to optimize team formation in large capstone programs. Our approach utilizes a multi-source data ingestion pipeline that aggregates structured surveys, code repositories, scheduling availability, and professional profiles to capture comprehensive student competencies. This data feeds into SkillNet, a dynamic knowledge graph integrated via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which maps raw inputs to a standardized skill ontology. Finally, OptiTeam, an LLM-based orchestration agent, translates these skill maps and instructor constraints expressed in natural language into mathematically optimized teams using Integer Linear Programming (ILP). By automating complex mathematical formulations within an isolated sandbox, this scalable architecture eliminates administrative bottlenecks, guarantees constraint satisfaction, and ensures equitable team dynamics across varying cohort sizes. The system provides an interactive dashboard, allowing instructors to audit assignments and express theoretically any grouping constraint they desire using everyday language.

- Independent replay of any claimed counterexample through a NumPy forward pass of the BNN: verify_counterexamples.py .

Title: To study endocrine manifestations in children and adolescents with thalassemia major a prospective cohort study

Description: Background: Thalassemia major is one of the most common hereditary hemoglobinopathies
worldwide, characterized by ineffective erythropoiesis and chronic hemolytic anemia. Regular
blood transfusions, though life-saving, result in progressive iron overload affecting various
organs including the endocrine glands. Despite advances in iron chelation therapy,
endocrinopathies remain a significant cause of morbidity in thalassemia major patients.
Objective: To study the endocrine manifestations in children and adolescents with thalassemia
major and to identify associated risk factors.
Methods: This study included 51 children and adolescents with thalassemia major attending the
thalassemia clinic. Detailed history, anthropometric assessment, clinical examination, and
laboratory investigations including complete blood count, serum ferritin, glucose parameters
(FBS, PPBS, RBS, HbA1c), thyroid function tests (T3, T4, TSH), serum calcium, and
gonadotropin levels (LH, FSH) were performed.
Results: The study population comprised 58.8% males and 41.2% females, with 62.7% aged 5
10 years. 74.5% had initiated transfusions before one year of age, and 88.2% received monthly
transfusions. Growth retardation was evident with 23.5% having weight and 29.4% having
height below the 3rd centile. Endocrine abnormalities included diabetes (25.5%), pre-diabetes
(33.3%), hypothyroidism (9.8%), hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (25% with low LH and
12.5% with low FSH), and hypocalcemia (21.6%). Serum ferritin was elevated (>1500 ng/mL) in
90.2% of patients. Significant associations were observed between HbA1c levels and chelation
therapy (p<0.001), hypogonadism with chelation therapy (p=0.005).

Title: Beyond Survival: Social, Emotional, and Identity Pathways into Illegal Drug Market Involvement in England

Description: This study explores the factors shaping involvement in drug markets, challenging assumptions that participation is primarily driven by financial gain. While economic factors remain significant, the findings demonstrate that involvement is also shaped by deeper social, emotional, and identity-based processes that extend beyond survival. Adopting a qualitative approach, the research draws on semi-structured interviews with individuals formerly involved in drug dealing, whose perspective remains underrepresented within existing literature. The findings show that involvement does not emerge from a single cause, but through the interaction between structural constraints, social environments, and individual experiences. Financial pressure, limited legitimate opportunities, peer influence, and neighbourhood contexts shaped initial involvement, while identity, status, masculinity, and emotional factors sustained engagement over time. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of drug market involvement and highlights the need for more effective responses that offer viable alternatives to criminal engagement. Existing punitive approaches and processes of marginalisation may reinforce social exclusion and limit access to legitimate opportunities. The findings support the need for preventative strategies that move beyond punitive and deterrence-based approaches by addressing the underlying social, structural, and emotional conditions associated with drug market involvement.

Title: Consistency of the Trojan Universality Class with Recent Observational Limits on Stable Earth Trojan Asteroids

Description: In this concise technical note, Doug Doucette demonstrates the compatibility between his Trojan Universality Class framework and the latest observational and numerical results on Earth Trojan asteroids from the Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST) campaign reported by Lu et al. (2026).

The Trojan Universality Class formalizes long-term confinement near elliptic–elliptic equilibria (such as the Sun–Earth L4 and L5 points) through a combination of a clear spectral gap between the two libration frequencies, a finite-order Birkhoff normal form depending only on actions, persistence of invariant KAM tori, and Nekhoroshev-type exponential bounds on action drift. This architecture, supported by Poisson-algebraic constraints, explains how local instability can coexist with long-term coherence in the vicinity of these Lagrange points.

The WFST survey covered 236.74 square degrees (about 33% of the stable orbital probability density derived from N-body integrations) but detected no new L4 Earth Trojans. It placed a 95% confidence upper limit of roughly 19 objects larger than ~520 m (for albedo 0.15). However, the supporting long-term N-body simulations (integrating test particles for up to 10^6–10^7 years) identified a substantial set of 57,261 stable orbits that remain confined near L4 for at least hundreds of thousands to millions of years. These stable trajectories exhibit a characteristic structured distribution: a dense core, diffuse halo, and a notable gap in inclination.

Doucette argues that these results align perfectly with the Trojan framework. The positive-measure set of long-lived confined orbits provides numerical confirmation of the persistence theorems (KAM + Nekhoroshev) at the heart of the class. The structured morphology matches expectations from the two-mode normal form and the protective role of the spectral gap, which prevents destructive low-order resonances. The non-detection and modest upper population limit constrain only the current number of detectable large bodies, not the underlying phase-space measure of stable regions. Known temporary co-orbitals (2010 TK7 and 2020 XL5) lie outside the long-term stable domain, consistent with the framework’s distinction between protected local confinement and chaotic temporary capture.

The note carefully acknowledges limitations: the survey does not directly measure frequencies, gap size, or action drifts; global N-body dynamics exceed the strict local normal-form approximation; and the results offer indirect rather than definitive validation. Nevertheless, no observational or numerical finding contradicts the structural hypotheses of the Trojan Universality Class. The framework remains a precise and applicable description of the local dynamics enabling long-term confinement near Earth’s triangular Lagrange points, with the WFST results supplying supportive empirical context.

Title: FROM CITY ASSETS TO PRODUCTIVE JOBS: AN EVENT-HISTORY FRAMEWORK FOR DIAGNOSING URBAN GROWTH CONSTRAINTS IN HISTORICAL CITIES

Description: This article develops a qualitative framework for diagnosing why the economic assets of secondary cities do
not always translate into productive investment, stable employment, and higher household earnings. It reformulates a field
instrument prepared for Kokand, Samarkand, and Khiva as an article-level research design. The central methodological
claim is that urban constraints should not be inferred from rankings of general problems. They should be reconstructed
through concrete, dated decisions in which an investor, worker, household, public agency, or service provider faced a
binding obstacle and altered behaviour as a result.
The framework combines seven respondent-specific interview protocols with a common event-history sequence. Each
interview begins with a real investment, hiring, connection, service, training, tourism, commuting, or household-enterprise
event. It then identifies the relevant actor and rule, reconstructs the order of actions, measures the associated shadow
price, records the workaround, compares the case with a less-exposed or successful case, and tests the response
expected if the constraint were relaxed. The unit of evidence is therefore a causal-process observation rather than an
unstructured opinion.
The comparative design links this evidence to five diagnostic pillars: market access; firm capabilities and business inputs;
labour allocation, skills, and inclusion; land, infrastructure, urban access, and amenities; and institutions, coordination,
and policy incidence. Common questions support comparison across the three cities, while targeted probes address
inherited industrial and craft capabilities in Kokand, tourism, development, and heritage pressures in Samarkand, and
water, sanitation, destination management, and seasonality in Khiva.
The article shows how the interview architecture can distinguish a binding constraint from a visible symptom. Credible
diagnosis requires convergence across actors, measurable costs or delays, behavioural responses, negative cases,
documentary corroboration, and a clear policy locus. The framework is intended for hypothesis testing and prioritisation
before large-scale policy design. It does not report completed fieldwork; instead, it establishes the analytical structure
through which field evidence can be converted into city-specific causal narratives and actionable reform propositions.

Title: Runway Incursion Prevention in UAE Airports Human and Technological barriers

Description: Runway incursion is recognized as one of the most dangerous safety hazards that can be encountered during airport operations. Hence, it is defined as the unexpected or invalid presence of an aircraft, vehicle, or personnel on an active runway. This typically results in devastating high-speed collisions and severe aviation tragedies. This research explores runway incursion risks and the preventative measures taken within the airports of the United Arab Emirates , a country that acts as a major global aviation hub of rapidly growing air traffic. Additionally, the study was completed using a qualitative research approach based on the analysis of previously published aviation literature, international safety reports, and an investigation case of a runway incursion in Dubai International Airport .

The findings of this report reveal that runway incursions are mainly caused by a series of human performance limitations, communication mishaps between pilots and air traffic controllers, and operational complications linked with airport ground navigation. Additionally, the research emphasizes the importance of implementing innovative technological systems such as surface movement radar, runway lighting systems, and advanced monitoring technologies that enhance situational awareness and vigilance, as well as runway safety risks. Lastly, the study concludes the research by presenting UAE's continuous efforts of implementing strong safety initiatives with the help of organizations like the National Runway Safety Team and the General Civil Aviation Authority , as well as regular improvements in training, communication protocols, airport layout, and technological monitoring systems crucial to further enhance runway safety and avoid future incursions.

This document provides a comprehensive description of the supplementary materials accompanying the manuscript entitled 'Digital Currency Fragmentation and Systemic Risk in the West African Monetary Zone: A Topological Data Analysis of Cross-Border Payment Network Spillovers.' The supplementary materials are organized into four categories: (i) primary data files, (ii) replication codes, (iii) generated figures, and (iv) computational environment specifications. All materials are designed to ensure full transparency, reproducibility, and independent verification of the empirical findings reported in the manuscript.

2. Data Files

The primary data file is provided in Microsoft Excel format (.xlsx) and contains four separate worksheets. Each worksheet corresponds to a distinct component of the empirical analysis. The file is named 'WAMZ_CBDC_TDA_Data.xlsx' and is available for download from the repository.

2.1 Sheet 1: WAMZ_Payment_Flows

This worksheet contains 600 rows of quarterly bilateral cross-border payment flow data for the West African Monetary Zone (WAMZ) covering the period 2015Q1 to 2024Q4 (40 quarters). The data integrate three primary sources: (i) SWIFT regional reports, (ii) West African Clearing House (WACH) settlement data, and (iii) mobile money corridor data from GSMA and individual mobile network operators (MTN, Airtel, Orange).

Variables:

· Quarter: String (e.g., '2015Q1'). Quarterly time identifier.

· Year: Integer. Calendar year (2015-2024).

· Quarter_Num: Integer (1-4). Quarter within the calendar year.

· Time_Index: Integer (0-39). Sequential quarter index for computational processing.

· Origin: String (3-letter code). Origin country: GHA, GMB, GUI, LBR, NGA, SLE.

· Destination: String (3-letter code). Destination country.

· Flow_USD_Millions: Float. Bilateral payment flow in USD millions, integrated from SWIFT, WACH, and mobile money sources.

· COVID_Period: Binary (0/1). Indicator for COVID-19 pandemic quarters (2020Q1-2021Q2).

· Ghana_CBDC_Pilot: Binary (0/1). Indicator for post-e-Cedi design paper quarters (>= 2021Q3).

Title: El Sueño de Libia

Description: El sueño de Libia / Chî Libia kamokarā is a bilingual illustrated children's book written in Spanish and Embera Chamí, the ancestral language of the Embera Chamí indigenous people of Colombia's Pacific region. The story follows Libia, a fictional eight-year-old Embera Chamí girl living in the Chocó and Risaralda departments, who navigates daily hunger, barefoot walks to school, and a family stretched to its limits — and who, each night, dreams of a life where food, warmth, and learning are simply given rights.

The book is a creative output derived from the doctoral research "En la cuna del hambre mi niño estaba": comprensión de la determinación social de la desnutrición aguda infantil en Chocó y Risaralda en 2024, estudio de caso comparado , conducted at the Facultad Nacional de Salud Pública, Universidad de Antioquia, Colombia. It translates the academic findings on the social determinants of acute child malnutrition among indigenous communities into an accessible literary format, drawing a deliberate line between the structural reality children face and the possibility of a dignified life — what Andean and Pacific communities call buen vivir .

The character Libia was named in honor of Libia Restrepo, the author's mother, who passed away during the writing of the thesis. The Embera Chamí translation was produced by Jorge Ulicer Vélez Osorio, an Embera teacher and community member residing in Marsella, Risaralda. The book was made possible through the financial support of WWB Foundation Colombia.

Title: SHARP: A Safe Hierarchical Agentic Resource Planner for Autonomous Multi-Cell 6G RAN Slicing

Description: Sixth-generation (6G) radio access networks (RANs) must allocate physical resource
blocks (PRBs) across network slices with competing service level agreements (SLAs), under a long-term
energy budget and a hard per-slot capacity limit. Existing learning-based slicing controllers soften these
constraints into penalties or trust regions, and therefore provide only asymptotic, in-expectation guarantees;
they converge slowly, offer no per-slot safety while the policy explores, and their action space grows
exponentially with the number of slices. This paper presents SHARP, a Safe Hierarchical Agentic Resource
Planner, realized as a hierarchical self-correcting controller that closes a plan-reason-act-monitor loop:
an intent interface decomposes operator intents into slice targets; a planning layer runs entropic online
mirror descent over decision frames; a verification layer couples a Lyapunov-driven virtual energy queue
with a safety projection onto the capacity set; a worker reserves capacity for ultra-reliable low-latency
communication (URLLC) traffic; and a monitor with key performance indicator (KPI) memory corrects the
controller online under capacity anomalies and falsified telemetry. The analysis establishes a deterministic
per-slot capacity guarantee; a throughput-energy tradeoff in which the optimality gap of the implemented
algorithm is B0/V + c1, that is, an O(1/V ) decaying term plus a fixed, state-independent design offset c1
that quantifies the price of the structural URLLC reservation and the conservative throttle, against O(V )
virtual-queue growth, with the offset derived in closed form and certified against an exact per-slot oracle; an
O(
p
T/H) manager regret; an exponential-to-polynomial complexity reduction; and a vanishing expected
power overshoot during learning. In a simulation study over eighteen alternatives and twenty seeds, SHARP
is the only method that combines zero URLLC violation with high energy feasibility, and it attains the
highest energy efficiency among the methods that meet the URLLC SLA while requiring no training
episodes. An equalized-safety-layer study attributes the nominal safety result precisely: the deterministic
reservation, throttle, and projection layer alone reproduces the zero-violation and energy-feasibility figures
at nominal stationary load, and the adaptive hierarchy and the monitor earn their place under drift, capacity
anomalies, and falsified telemetry rather than at nominal steady state. Within the same simulation model,
its safety behavior is retained through event-driven attack scenarios and carries over without retraining to
unseen topologies, offered loads, and networks of one hundred cells. The components map onto the O-RAN
architecture, and the profiled per-decision compute time of the controller is 132 to 262 microseconds. All
quantitative results are outputs of the stated system-level simulation model of the abstracted traffic, channel,
and power dynamics; no hardware or testbed measurements are claimed.

Title: Organizational Mechanics of Effective Cardinality Transitions

Description: This paper develops a mathematical framework for \emph{organizational
mechanics}: the mechanics by which physical systems reorganize state spaces,
basins, constraints, degeneracies, barriers, and relaxation spectra in order
to accelerate computation without thereby exceeding the computability limits
of finite computable physics.

The central distinction is between literal Cantorian cardinality and
\emph{effective distinguishable cardinality}. Reversible deterministic
dynamics and unitary quantum dynamics preserve literal cardinality, but phase
transitions, symmetry breaking, constraint activation, quotienting,
reservoir coupling, and degeneracy reshaping can alter operational state
counts such as
\[
N_\eps(\XX,d),\qquad
\dim \HH_{\rm eff},\qquad
h_{\rm top},\qquad
\text{metastable basin count},\qquad
\log g_i.
\]
Within the usual bounded weak-gravity Bekenstein regime, distinguishable
information is bounded by
\[
\log_2 N_{\rm distinguishable}
\le
\Beken(E,R)
:=
\frac{2\pi E R}{\hbar c\ln 2}.
\]
Therefore every effective-cardinality increase in a bounded physical system
must be understood as use of pre-existing unused capacity, import of boundary
or reservoir information, degradation of resolution elsewhere, or increase of
physical resources.

The central object of the paper is an organizational state
\[
\Org_\theta
=
(\XX,\PPc_\theta,G_\theta,E_\theta,g_\theta,B_\theta,\RRR_\theta),
\]
where \(\PPc_\theta\) is a partition into macrostates or basins,
\(G_\theta\) is a transition graph, \(E_\theta\) basin energies,
\(g_\theta\) degeneracies, \(B_\theta\) barriers, and
\(\RRR_\theta\) a readout. An organization method is a controlled
transformation of this tuple: restriction, quotient, refinement, coarsening,
degeneracy dilation, barrier reshaping, energetic tilt, reservoir lift, graph
rewiring, or readout change. Such transformations induce stochastic
computation channels of the form
\[
\Comp_{\theta,t}
=
\MM_\theta\,\ee^{tK_\theta^\ast}\,\PPc_\theta,
\]
or quantum analogues.

The Mpemba effect becomes a central organizing mechanism. For a reversible
finite Markov relaxation semigroup,
\[
p_t(i)
=
\pi_i\left[
1+\sum_{k\ge1}c_k(p_0)\phi_k(i)\ee^{-\lambda_k t}
\right],
\]
where \(\phi_k\) are eigenfunctions of the backward generator. A strong
Mpemba effect occurs when
\[
c_1(p_0)=0,
\]
removing the slowest relaxation mode. With basin degeneracies
\(g_i(\lambda)\), thermal initial states have weights
\[
p_i(\beta,\lambda)
=
\frac{g_i(\lambda)\ee^{-\beta E_i(\lambda)}}{Z(\beta,\lambda)}.
\]
Thus degeneracy or basin-cardinality transitions can create, move, or destroy
Mpemba surfaces
\[
c_1(\beta,\lambda)=0.
\]
A general convex-geometric criterion is proved: for eigenfunction spectral
points
\[
\Phi_i=(\phi_1(i),\dots,\phi_r(i))\in\RR^r,
\]
there exist degeneracies producing an order-\(r\) Mpemba state if and only if
\[
0\in\conv\{\Phi_i\}.
\]
A fully solved three-basin model is also given, with explicit generator,
stationary distribution, eigenfunctions, Mpemba temperature, chi-square
relaxation law, observable signatures, and acceleration factor
\[
\mathcal S\sim\frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1}.
\]

Finally, the paper formalizes the hypercomputation obstruction. If energy,
radius, run time, preparation, dynamics, and measurement precision are
recursively bounded and computable at finite resolution, then the physical
computer computes only recursive functions. Hypercomputation requires at
least one escape hatch: unbounded Bekenstein capacity, infinite time,
infinite precision, noncomputable parameters, noncomputable dynamics, or a
nonuniform oracle-like device family. Phase transitions and Mpemba
acceleration can reorganize and accelerate computation, but within finite
computable physics they do not by themselves compute nonrecursive functions.
The central conclusion is a separation theorem: organization can change the
effective computational landscape and the relaxation spectrum, but under
finite computable resources it cannot change the recursive/nonrecursive
boundary.

Title: Rumbler: A Reverb-Based Feedback Instrument

Description: We present the Rumbler, a feedback instrument that harnesses acoustic reverberation to generate complex, unpredictable sounds. A microphone and speaker are mounted to opposite ends of a tube. As the tube is stretched and compressed, the acoustic space within it changes, amplifying different resonant frequencies and altering the resulting pitch. The Rumbler also features four force-sensing resistors, a mouse scroll wheel, and a 9DOF sensor, which can be mapped to various audio filters. These controls modify the audio feedback, enhancing the instrument's expressiveness and sonic complexity. We discuss strategies and considerations for mapping filters for the Rumbler and detail two particular mappings that were used for live performance. We share our reflections on the success and limitations of these mappings. Finally, given that the Rumbler can sustain sound without any audio input, we explore the connection between the Rumbler and no-input mixing and its implication for future practice and performance.

The cross section is very poorly preserved, with fungi visible in vessels. Growth rings are absent. Wood is diffuse-porous. Vessels are solitary (37 %) or in radial multiples of 2 (37 %), 3 (18 %), 4 (5 %), 5 (1%) (Fig. 4A). Vessels are rounded in outline or slightly oval. Mean tangential diameter of 90 µm, range 76-103 µm, 11-16 per mm². Perforation plates are exclusively simple; intervessel-pits are alternate, minute, less than 4 µm and densely distributed (Fig. 4E); vessel-ray pits are indistinct. Vessel wall thickness is about 9 µm. Vessel element length is not distinct.
Rays are 2-3 seriate with short uniseriate ends, uniseriate rays are rare, 6-8 per mm, heterocellular, composed of procumbent body cells with 1-4 or more than 4 rows of square and upright cells. Ray height range is between 157-421 µm (11-37 cells); width is between 17-21 µm. Gum or other deposits are present in vessels (Fig. 4C, D). Axial parenchyma is confluent, anastomosed in irregular and wavy bands. Parenchyma strands are composed of 3-4 or 5-8 cells. Fibres are septate or not septate, with diameter range of 9-18 µm, medium to thick-walled; pits are not observed. Mineral inclusions are visible in all ray cells and in parenchyma (Fig. 4D).
AFFINITIES AND COMPARISONS
The combination of diffuse-porous wood, with randomly arranged vessels, minute-small vessel-pits, predominantly paratracheal parenchyma that is vasicentric to slightly aliform, predominantly triseriate rays composed of heterocellular cells, and chambered crystalliferous axial parenchyma occur commonly in the Combretaceae or Fabaceae. Due to it’s poor preservation, the fossil cannot be identified more precisely than Combretaceae / Fabaceae gen. and sp. indet. 1.

 Patients underwent pre-anesthetic evaluation with detailed history, airway examination, and systemic

Description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming medical diagnostics, offering fundamentally new approaches to clinical data analysis. This article, based on an analysis of current scientific publications, examines the potential and limitations of implementing AI systems in clinical practice. Advances in medical imaging, disease prognosis, and clinical decision support are analyzed, as well as critical challenges related to the methodological quality of studies, model interpretability, integration into clinical workflows, and ethical aspects. REFERRED SPECIMENS. — USNM 16638, USNM 16639, FMNH PM-459, USNM MMNS VP 130.
DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS. — Dorudon serratus can be separated from Dorudon atrox by the following features: the lack of an anterior process on the frontals in adult specimens (this study); the presence of an extra mesial accessory denticle on dP2, three in total (Uhen 2004); a weaker lingual projection on the dP3 and dP4 (Andrews’s posterointernal buttress; Uhen 2004) the presence of large vertebroarterial foramina on the mid-cervical vertebrae (diameter greater than the upper bounding bony rim; this study).
DISCUSSION
The type of D. serratus consists of teeth, skull fragments and some vertebrae from a juvenile individual (Kellogg 1936; Uhen 2013a). The species has mostly remained restricted to the type species (Kellogg 1936), but additional specimens of D. serratus were recognized by Uhen (2013a), including MMAS A and MMNS VP 130. These reassignments were based on dental morphology (Uhen pers. comm.). Dental differences between D. serratus and Zy. kochii have emerged as the main diagnostic feature separating the two taxa in existing literature. The diagnostic feature for D. serratus being the presence of a smaller, non-crenulated cingulum on the upper premolars. These premolars are not present in USNM 16638, USNM 16639, and FMNH PM-459, meaning this feature cannot be used to diagnose these specimens. Instead, relying on the posterior narial region, USNM 16639 is nearly identical to that of MMNS VP 130, it seems more likely this specimen belongs to D. serratus . FMNH PM-459 possesses neither upper premolars, not a posterior narial region, but does possess a more rounded nuchal crest and double rooted p1 like MMNS VP 130, and USNM 16639. USNM 16638 possesses deciduous dentition, allowing for direct comparison with the holotype of D. serratus . Uhen (2013a) described a more prominent cingulum on the dP2-4 of this specimen as compared to MCZ 8763, however only Kellogg (1936) mentions a slight cinguloid ridge on the labial surface below the distal two denticles of dP 3 in his description of the deciduous dentition of USNM 16638. No mention of any cingulum is given in any of the other described teeth. Suggesting the difference is based only on a slight difference in cingulum on one tooth. Given the number of crenulated cingula differs between USNM 11962, and MSC 3927 (Daly 1999), it seems that this difference can be related to intraspecific variation. More detailed assessments of dental morphology are needed to say for certain what the meaning of these differences is. Diagnostic cranial differences between Zygorhiza kochii and Dorudon serratus are given in Figure 7. The vertebral proportions of basilosaurids are considered highly diagnostic (Uhen 2005; Gingerich 2007; Uhen 2013a; Martínez-Cáceres et al. 2017). Uhen (2004; 2013a) states that Zygorhiza possesses vertebrae slightly smaller and less robust than those of Dorudon spp. When we compared the vertebral lengths of specimens from Chrysocetus healyorum , Dorudon serratus and Zygorhiza kochii we did not find significant differences correlating with skull morphology (Fig. 8). The most major interspecific difference is the small size of the C. healyorum holotype, however this specimen is also a juvenile (Uhen & Gingerich 2001). Thus, it is not clear if this difference is actually taxonomically informative. Instead, the most major variation was found in the posterior thoracic, lumbar, and anterior caudal vertebrae. With this exception, all specimens possess similarly sized cervicals and anterior thoracics, after which a pattern of stepwise increasing variation is seen moving posteriorly across the torso series (viz. Buchholtz 2001: posterior thoracic, lumbar, and anterior caudal vertebrae). AUMP 2368 (associated with the skull MSC 3927), possesses the shortest vertebrae, diverging from the other specimens midway through the thoracic series. USNM 4678 and USNM 12063 only diverge at the posteriormost thoracic vertebrae. The longest lumbars are seen in MMNS VP 130 and USNM 4679.
DESCRIPTION OF SPECIMEN TM 8501
TM 8501 consists of a skull, mandibles, and some associated postcrania including portions of seven vertebrae, three ribs, two sternebrae and a partial basihyal. None of the appendicular skeleton was recovered. Based on the completed dental eruption and fused epiphyses on vertebrae, TM 8501 represents a mature individual. Title: The Topographic Writing of Women's Lives into the Sacred Landscape of the Argolid

Description: This science communication article explores how ancient Greek societies utilized their physical environment to regulate women’s lives, sexuality, and reproduction . Focusing on the Argolid region, the study applies the anthropological concept of "topographic writing" to demonstrate that the natural landscape served as a legible canvas for social control and collective memory . Rather than relying solely on civil laws, the ancient polis embedded biopolitical regulations—such as marriage and legitimate lineage—into sacred topographies and religious rituals overseen by deities like Aphrodite . Through specific case studies, the research decodes the 'topograms' of the Argolid, including embodied prenuptial hair offerings to Hippolytus in Troezen, the reproductive regulatory node of Aphrodite’s temple in Hermione for both brides and widows, and the ritualized gender subversion of the Hybristika festival in Argos . These sacred spaces and practices functioned as a panoptic tool, transforming strict patriarchal norms into unquestionable divine laws . Ultimately, reading the mnemohistory inscribed in the landscape allows the HIEROTOPOI project to move beyond male-centric historical narratives, successfully recovering the marginalized, lived experiences of ancient women .

This publication is part of the digital outreach and knowledge transfer strategy for the HIEROTOPOI project (10.55776/PAT2141125).

Title: Zwischen Autonomie und didaktischer Anleitung

Description: Abstract

Generative AI has become a routine companion in secondary computing education, yet unguided access to ready-made solutions threatens the very learning processes that project-based learning (PjBL) is designed to foster. This thesis investigates how the degree of didactic guidance built into an AI tutor affects teaching and learning in project-based programming instruction.

Methodology

In a five-week quasi-experimental mixed-methods field study, 49 ninth-grade students at an Austrian technical secondary school completed physical computing projects (using the Raspberry Pi Pico and MicroPython) under one of two conditions:

- A didactically guided, Socratic AI tutor configured to withhold complete solutions (complemented by an AI reflection journal capable of asking probing questions).

- Unguided AI access (accompanied by a traditional worksheet for reflection).

Both conditions were provided on the same GDPR-compliant platform. Three data levels were triangulated:

- Focus groups with teachers and pre-service teachers ( N = 12, evaluative qualitative content analysis, 208 codings).

- 374 logged chat sessions comprising 2,665 prompts (quantitative log analysis and structuring qualitative content analysis).

- A standardized post-test ( N = 40).

Results

Teachers judged AI use strictly by project phase, endorsing only guided scaffolding while insisting that creative ideation remain AI-free and rejecting AI process data as a basis for summative assessment.

The process data reveal that restriction changed how , not whether , students used AI: guided groups interacted more frequently, requested ready-made code significantly less often ( p = .047, r = -.83), engaged in more co-constructive dialogue, and produced a more than threefold higher share of analytical reflection ( p = .030, r = .44).

Experience measures (support quality, cognitive load, perceived learning) did not differ between conditions; however, 38.1% of students with guided access categorically rejected AI tutors as harmful, compared to 5.3% with free access ( p = .021). This dissociation is interpreted as psychological reactance to perceived paternalism rather than as a consequence of a poorer experience.

Conclusion

The findings converge on a model of qualitative dosing: restrict solution generation rather than access, calibrate the restriction to project phase and prior knowledge, and communicate it as a justified pedagogical structure. Practical guidelines for configuring and framing AI tutors in K-12 computing education are derived.

Keywords: Generative AI, Computing Education, Project-Based Learning, AI Tutors, Secondary Education, K-12

Title: The Market for Attention: Platform Architecture, Download Friction, and the Download-to-View Ratio in Cross-Listed Scholarly Papers

Description: This paper examines the download-to-view ratio for 169 scholarly papers held simultaneously on SSRN and Zenodo, using the cross-listed structure as a natural experiment in which the work is held constant and only the platform varies. The central finding is that the same paper exhibits a usage ratio 2.49 times higher on Zenodo than on SSRN (paired median ratio; 95% bootstrap CI 2.23 to 2.70; geometric-mean ratio 2.60; Hodges-Lehmann 2.58). Zenodo's ratio exceeds SSRN's for 108 of 111 papers in a conservative single-file subset (paired Wilcoxon p = 1.1 x 10^-19; rank-biserial 0.99; paired Cohen's d_z = 1.81 on the log-ratio), and the direction holds across natural sciences, engineering, and social sciences. Because the work is held constant, no property of the work can explain the difference. The paper argues that the effect is not primarily behavioral but a case of measurement noninvariance: SSRN and Zenodo do not define a "view" or a "download" equivalently, so their usage ratios are not the same quantity and are not directly comparable. Several non-exclusive mechanisms are consistent with the gap, including asymmetric counting rules (Zenodo counting file previews and direct-link downloads, SSRN filtering anonymous downloads from its counted total), differing download friction, and differing user-intent profiles; the data narrow but do not fully identify their relative contributions. A secondary hypothesis, that the gap would be modulated by title technicality, returns a null (beta = -0.10, p = 0.12), though with a placeholder technicality measure that limits its weight. The download-to-view ratio, treated in the scientometrics literature as a property of the paper, is better understood as a joint product of the paper and the platform's measurement architecture, and is not portable across platforms without explicit adjustment.

Title: AI for Holistic Medicine: Understanding Multi-Organ Interactions in Cancers

Description: Cancer is no longer viewed as a disease confined to a single organ. Modern research shows that tumors influence the immune system, metabolism, hormones, blood vessels, microbiome, and distant organs throughout the body. This broader perspective has encouraged the development of holistic and systems-based medicine, where physicians and researchers attempt to understand cancer as a dynamic network of interactions rather than an isolated mass of abnormal cells. Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming a critical tool in this transformation because it can analyze enormous and complex biological datasets that humans alone cannot fully interpret. Traditional oncology often focused on a single tumor site, such as breast, lung, or colon cancer. However, cancer progression depends on communication between multiple organs and biological systems. For example, liver metabolism can influence drug effectiveness, the gut microbiome can affect immune responses, and chronic inflammation in one organ may accelerate tumor growth elsewhere. Metastasis itself is a multi-organ process in which cancer cells travel through the bloodstream and colonize distant tissues. AI-driven holistic medicine aims to map these interconnected pathways and reveal patterns that may improve diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment planning. One of the most important contributions of AI in holistic cancer medicine is the integration of “multi-omics” data. Multi-omics refers to combining information from genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and epigenomics to create a comprehensive picture of disease biology. Each layer provides different insights into how cancer behaves. Genomics identifies DNA mutations, transcriptomics examines gene activity, proteomics studies proteins, and metabolomics tracks chemical changes in cells and organs. AI algorithms can merge these data sources to identify hidden relationships that may not be visible through conventional statistical methods. Machine learning and deep learning models are especially valuable because cancer datasets are extremely large and multidimensional. AI systems can detect subtle molecular signatures associated with treatment resistance, early metastasis, or organ-specific complications. For example, researchers now use AI to study how tumors interact with the immune system and distant organs during disease progression. These models help predict which patients are likely to respond to immunotherapy, chemotherapy, or targeted drugs. In precision oncology, AI can also personalize treatments by matching therapies to a patient’s unique biological profile. Another emerging area is AI-assisted radiomics, which combines medical imaging with molecular analysis. Advanced AI models can extract thousands of hidden imaging features from CT scans, MRI scans, and PET scans. When combined with multi-omics data, these imaging insights help physicians understand how tumors affect surrounding tissues and distant organs. AI-driven radiomics may allow clinicians to monitor disease spread earlier and evaluate systemic effects without invasive procedures. Holistic medicine also emphasizes the importance of lifestyle, nutrition, and environmental factors in cancer care. AI can analyze longitudinal patient data, including diet, physical activity, wearable sensor data, microbiome composition, and medication history. By integrating these variables, AI systems may identify how external factors contribute to cancer progression or recovery. Researchers believe this approach could support preventive medicine and reduce the side effects of aggressive cancer therapies. Recent advances in systems biology further support the idea of multi-organ AI models. Scientists are developing “digital twin” frameworks that simulate the biological behavior of individual patients across multiple organs and physiological systems. These computational models may eventually predict how cancer evolves over time and how treatments influence the entire body rather than a single tumor. Early research into multi-organ AI endophenotypes has already demonstrated how AI can identify shared disease mechanisms across the brain, heart, eyes, and cancer-related pathways. Despite its promise, AI in holistic cancer medicine still faces challenges. Data privacy, algorithm bias, limited clinical validation, and difficulties integrating hospital systems remain major barriers. Many AI models also function as “black boxes,” making it difficult for physicians to fully understand their reasoning. Nevertheless, ongoing research continues to improve transparency and reliability. In the future, AI may transform oncology from a reactive discipline into a predictive and preventive science. By understanding cancer as a multi-organ and system-wide disease, holistic AI-driven medicine has the potential to improve early detection, personalize treatment, reduce side effects, and enhance patient outcomes. The combination of AI, systems biology, and multi-omics research is therefore shaping a new era of precision and holistic cancer care.

Title: Cuidados de Enfermagem Às Mulheres em Situação de Violência Doméstica e Familiar à Luz da Lei Maria da Penha: Revisão Integrativa

Description: A violência doméstica e familiar contra a mulher constitui grave problema de saúde pública e violação dos direitos humanos, com repercussões físicas, psicológicas, sexuais, morais, patrimoniais e sociais. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar os cuidados de enfermagem evidenciados na literatura científica para a assistência às mulheres em situação de violência doméstica e familiar, à luz da Lei Maria da Penha. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, de abordagem qualitativa e caráter descritivo, realizada nas bases SciELO, LILACS, BDENF e BVS, com apoio complementar de normativas oficiais consultadas no Site Oficial do Planalto. Foram incluídos artigos em português, disponíveis na íntegra, publicados entre 2020 e 2026, relacionados aos cuidados de enfermagem às mulheres em situação de violência doméstica e familiar. Os achados foram organizados em cinco categorias temáticas: acolhimento humanizado e escuta qualificada; identificação de sinais físicos, psicológicos, sexuais e sociais da violência; registro e notificação compulsória; encaminhamento à rede intersetorial de proteção; e fragilidades enfrentadas pela Enfermagem nesse cuidado. Conclui-se que a atuação da Enfermagem deve ultrapassar o atendimento pontual às lesões físicas, assumindo uma perspectiva integral, ética, humanizada e articulada à rede de proteção, contribuindo para a segurança, autonomia e dignidade das mulheres.

Introduction: The Dielectric Geometry of Information

Classical computational theory has long been predicated on the temporal execution of sequential logic. From the earliest formalized Turing machines to modern von Neumann architectures, computation is universally modeled as an iterative, chronological evolution of states: . However, a rigorous mathematical and physical analysis reveals that this sequential "forward stream" is merely an artifact of the coordinate system chosen by an external observer. When computation is reframed as a geometric and topological structure, the concepts of time, algorithmic delay, and computational complexity cease to be fundamental physical laws. Instead, they emerge as projections of spatial coupling.

The foundational axiom of this framework requires examining the boundary conditions between two active processes—specifically, a reading process and a writing process. In any computational or physical system, a dielectric gap—a structural delay or separation—is geometrically required only when a reader and a writer are topologically "facing" one another, or when one is nested within the other. Two processes running in parallel without information exchange require no physical or temporal separation; they merely coexist without interaction. But the moment these processes couple—when the write mechanism directly feeds the read mechanism—a dielectric gap becomes structurally mandatory to prevent a degenerate short circuit.

This short circuit is the mathematical equivalent of evaluating in zero time, yielding an infinite, unresolvable loop that computes nothing. In nested systems, where an internal computational model operates inside the external environment it seeks to represent, the dielectric gap is the sole boundary maintaining the distinction between the model and the modeled reality. Title: Geometric Containment of Nonlinear Instability

Description: This paper formalizes geometric containment of nonlinear instability as the operational regime in which local chaos remains transport-limited relative to a declared coherent region and failure scale on a finite timescale. Local instability, diagnosed by a positive finite-time Lyapunov exponent, is a property of the tangent dynamics along a trajectory. Operational confinement is a property of phase-space geometry. The two are independent: exponential separation of nearby orbits does not by itself imply that an uncertainty envelope will reach the boundary that defines loss of coherence.

Within the Trojan normal-form setting developed in related work, containment is realized by a spectral-gap-protected, near-integrable skeleton. An elliptic–elliptic equilibrium whose linear frequencies satisfy a finite-order non-resonance condition admits a Birkhoff normal form whose truncated part is integrable. Residual invariant tori, cantori, and narrow resonant layers confine chaotic motion to thin stochastic bands whose diameter in the relevant transport coordinate remains much smaller than the distance to the failure boundary. The resulting thinness ratio stays strictly less than one, typically of order 10−2 10^{-2} 1 0 −2 or smaller. Nekhoroshev-type estimates further bound action drift on exponentially long intervals while the gap and remainder hypotheses persist.

Thin chaos is the typical contained state: positive Lyapunov exponents coexist with geometric isolation of the chaotic component. Weak and strong chaos classify the magnitude of the instability rate; thin and thick chaos classify its transport consequence. These axes are independent. Containment is maintained by spectral protection that excludes low-order resonances, by barrier integrity that limits flux, by the continued validity of a two-mode reduction, and by averaging that converts non-resonant coupling into slow residual drift.

Loss of containment occurs through an exhaustive hierarchy of structural exits—separatrix splitting, resonance overlap, spectral-gap collapse, or activation of additional modes—that exhaust the ways the Trojan defining conditions can fail. The passage from thin to thick chaos is therefore a connectivity transition: isolated chaotic layers become linked by non-negligible flux to the failure region. Any claim of operational nonlinear stability must therefore include a transport-sensitive diagnostic; a purely local instability measure is insufficient. The entire construction applies only to systems that admit the Trojan architectural signature and is always relative to an explicitly chosen coherent region, failure scale, and timescale.

Title: Geo3D-AI-CSU/STA-Indexing: STA-Indexing v1.0

Description: Three-dimensional (3D) geothermal numerical simulation is a key technique for resource assessment and development planning, which generates massive volumes of simulation data with multiple spatiotemporal physical attributes, such as temperature, pressure, and Darcy velocity vectors. Efficient retrieval of such 3D simulation database under combined spatial, temporal, and attribute constraints remains a major challenge. To address this challenge, this study proposes a spatio-temporal-attribute unified indexing method, STA-Indexing, on geothermal 3D numerical simulation databases. The method is designed for both 3D scattered points and structured voxels, and it supports three representative attribute types of categorical, scalar, and vector attributes. We use a single rowkey as the unified index to execute complex queries. Its prefix encodes attribute, spatial, and temporal information, while its suffix stores a unique identifier for each record. To support different data structures, the method adopts spatial encoding based on space-filling curves and multilevel grids, and also uses a two-level temporal encoding scheme to improve physical ordering efficiency. Performance experiments are conducted on databases of different scales. The results show that the proposed method consistently outperforms traditional incremental filtering, especially in large-scale scenarios. It achieves lower query latency and higher query efficiency for a variety of multidimensional query tasks. This methodology provides an efficient data retrieval support for geothermal digital platforms and intelligent energy management systems.

Description: This paper examines how multinational corporations integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) criteria into their long-term growth and production diversification strategies, departing from traditional international business models that prioritized labor arbitrage and logistical optimization. Title: WUR Mass Spectral Library

Description: On this webpage it is possible to download a high-resolution tandem mass spectral library entirely built at Wageningen University and Research (WUR) through the analysis of high-quality standards. The WUR Mass Spectral Library provides high-quality, manually curated data for a large collection of compounds of interest for multiple scientific fields of study.

The WUR Mass Spectral Library is a collaboration between multiple Wageningen Research institutes and Wageningen University chair groups including, Laboratory of Food Chemistry, Environmental Technology and Wageningen Food Safety Research.

This library is a collection of > 1,300 chemicals among which veterinary drugs, contaminants, pesticides, natural toxins, pharmaceuticals, food-derived small molecules and plant compounds (including metabolites). It was built using an ultra -high-pressure liquid chromatography (UHPLC) system coupled to an Orbitrap IQ-X Tribrid, with positive and negative ESI as the ionization interface depending on the chemical. MSn spectra of all compounds were recorded using HCD fragmentation (5-7 collision energy levels). MSn spectra of food-derived small molecules and plant compounds were also recorded using UVPD fragmentation (3 activation times). The library (> 9,000 mass spectra) can be used for:

Expanding compound annotations
Enables exact matches of compounds through high-quality spectral matching (level 2 identification), which can be combined with retention time (RT) information (level 1 identification), ensuring accurate compound identification.

Targeted and Suspect Screening
Easily implemented in your targeted and suspect screening workflows, improving detection capabilities for specific compounds.

Non-Target Screening
Assists in identifying unknown or analogous compounds in non-target screening, by integrating it with machine learning tools to detect novel compounds.

Please see WUR Website link for additional information and to request download access.

Additional information

Besides the complete WUR Mass Spectral Library, the spectra are also separately available based on their main relevant field of study. All libraries are available in both .db and .msp file format. Details on the methodology can be found in the articles mentioned in the citation instructions section, which will be expanded in the future. Please find the description of each library available through this page below:

- WUR mass spectral library pos/neg - Complete collection of spectra of over 1300 chemicals recorded in positive mode and over 475 chemicals recorded in negative mode at multiple collision energies (HCD) and/or multiple activiation times (UVPD) using RP-UHPLC-MS. The WUR mass spectral library contains all spectra mentioned below, with exception of hte polar substances library spectra.

- WFSR food safety mass spectral library pos/neg - Collection of spectra recorded at multiple collision energies (HCD) using RP-UHPLC-MS that are especially relevant for the field of food safety.

- WFSR polar substances mass spectral library pos/neg - Collection of spectra recorded at multiple collision energies (HCD) using flow injection for polar chemicals that are especially relevant for the field of food safety.

Note that for this library no noise levels were applied to the spectra since low intensity UVPD-fragments might be relevant. All chemicals in this library are either commercially available standards or purified and/or synthesized chemicals verified by NMR analysis.

- ETE organic environmental pollutants mass spectral library pos/neg - Collection of spectra recorded at multiple collision energies (HCD) using RP-UHPLC-MS for organic environmental pollutants that are especially relevant for the field of environmental analysis.

Title: Poisonous Plants Detection Using Deep Learning

Description: Abstract: Identifying poisonous plants in natural environments is often difficult, yet it is important for protecting both human health and animals. Traditional methods mainly depend on human observation, which can be slow and sometimes unreliable, especially when plants look similar. In this work, we created our own dataset consisting of 1,500 leaf images from seven poisonous plant species. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was then trained to classify these plants based on their leaf characteristics. To improve the learning process, the images were preprocessed and augmented. Instead of relying only on accuracy, the model was evaluated using additional measures such as precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrix analysis to better understand its performance. The model achieved a validation accuracy of about 87%, showing that deep learning can be useful for this task. This study provides a dataset, a baseline model, and an evaluation approach that can be useful for future research. Further improvements can be made by increasing the dataset size, using advanced models, and developing practical applications for real-world use.
